label: canon-fdi-rgate-n6
_why: FINDINGS F178 (2026-09-30). The user: bring Britain's U* (incl. peasants) up a bit so depeasantation is not the norm, and give a GBR player more challenge; go-ahead for probes + 6 full runs on configs of the agent's choice, no new game started after 16:00 local 2026-09-30. F178 showed the ladder levers (A, B, cost slope, trade) are ONE axis at ~4-5 years of Britain's depeasantation per 10% of world GDP, and world GDP already sits at vanilla's (median 1.03), so the batch tests an OFF-axis lever instead: CAPITAL EXPORT. Vanilla weights a foreign private investment in manufacturing at 0.25 (mines 1.0, plantations 1.25) and British capital barely leaves Britain in either game (5-568 levels owned abroad at 1935 against 10-31k at home). Raised to 1.0. Layered on it, for the player: the DATE GATE on the research journal entries (an industry entry for a game-era 3/4/5 technology grants half before 1855/1885/1920), whose AI side is expected to be neutral (research levers moved nothing downstream in F102/F107/F165) and is read on the tech-leader shares at the anchor years. The labour-light top rung of F178's proposal was DROPPED before launch: 75-80% of e2/e3 levels already run vanilla's labour-saving methods, which at the top rung remove every laborer, so halving base staffing would drive laborers negative.

_predictions.capital_export: PRE-REGISTERED 2026-09-30 01:20 local, before launch. (1) The mechanism: GBR's levels owned abroad at 1935 >= 5x the dam runs' (5-369, median ~70) in at least 4 of 6 runs; the other leaders' likewise; most of it manufacturing in labour-rich markets (the Indian subjects, the Americas). If owned-abroad levels do not move (the engine's investment-rights or domestic-bias plumbing binds first), the arm reads as the canon and the lever is null. (2) If it moves: Britain's end-state U* median 9% -> 12-16%, first year under 10% (non-stuck) 1929 -> 1934 or later; pool U* up toward its >= 2 aim; world GDP median inside 0.95-1.10 (capital moving to idle labour is not a GDP cost); world W up, world U* down; the capital-abundance runoffs rarer (a hoard can vent abroad). The stuck-Britain rate is not predicted to change (a pre-1880 mechanism).
_predictions.date_gate: AI leaders' share of each game era's technologies at its anchor year within 5 points of the dam runs' (1875 era 3 ~51%, 1905 era 4 ~46%, 1936 era 5 ~46% all trees); a handful of PMR_JEG|reduced lines per run (AI early adopters, mostly era 3 before 1855 and era 4 before 1885); nothing downstream attributable to it.

_correction: 2026-09-30 07:30, after launch (the running batch holds its own copy of this file): the premise and prediction (1) cite owned_abroad_levels, which counts GOVERNMENT ownership only. With every owner type resolved (financial districts, company HQs, manor houses) Britain owns 3.8k-11.5k levels abroad at 1936 in canon and vanilla runs alike, mostly mines, trade centres, railways and plantations; factories are ~0.2k-1.7k. The arm therefore tests a shift in COMPOSITION (factories abroad), read from the melted endpoint saves; FINDINGS F178 section 2.
